newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Apr housing completions fell 0.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Apr housing completions fell 0.1 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department report on completions of new privately-owned housing units, seasonally adjusted annual rates, in 1,000s, with percent changes from prior months and year over year.
Housing completions by region, seasonally adj., in 1,000s:

Commerce said April completions of single-family homes rose 0.1 percent after a revised 9.1 percent drop in March and a revised 14.2 percent increase in February. Previously, the department said single-family completions fell 12.0 percent in March and increased 13.4 percent in February.

April multi-family unit completions fell 1.0 percent after a revised 2.0 percent decline in March and a 20.6 percent increase in February. The department revised March multi-family unit completions from a 3.9 percent drop.

The department said actual completions on an unadjusted basis rose in April to 108,200 units from 108,000 units in March and from 104,800 units in February. In April 1996, actual completions were reported at 101,900 units.

Privately-owned housing units under construction in April were at a seasonally adjusted 817,000 units, matching the March total, but were down from 821,000 units in February. They compare with 825,000 units under construction in April 1996.
